title: Tanzanian Vegetable Coconut Stew
community: Swahili coast — the complete coastal vegetable dish
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Mboga za Nazi — a medley of seasonal vegetables simmered in a rich coconut milk sauce with Zanzibar spices. The coastal complete vegetable dish — where inland Tanzania uses peanuts for richness, the coast uses coconut milk.
longDesc: Mboga za Nazi is the coastal Tanzanian answer to any question about what to make with mixed vegetables — simmer them in coconut milk with Zanzibar spices and the result will always be magnificent. The coconut milk elevates every vegetable it touches.
steps: Heat oil. Cook onions until golden.
Add garlic, ginger, and spices. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes until thick.
Add sweet potato and carrot. Stir to coat. Cook 2 minutes.
Add coconut milk. Bring to gentle simmer.
Add green beans and eggplant. Simmer 8 minutes.
Add spinach. Stir until wilted — 1 minute.
chefTips: Add vegetables in order of cooking time — hardest first.
Spinach goes in at the very end — it wilts in seconds.
commonMistakes: Adding all vegetables simultaneously — uneven cooking.
cookingScience: Each vegetable in this stew reaches optimal doneness at different times. Staggered addition ensures all are perfectly cooked when the dish is served — neither mushy sweet potato nor raw spinach.
sustainabilityTips: A mixed vegetable stew uses whatever is seasonal and available — the most sustainable approach.
culturalNote: Mboga za Nazi is the Swahili coast's most versatile dish — the vegetables change with the season but the coconut milk-spice base remains constant. It is the dish that proves the Swahili coast philosophy: coconut milk makes everything better.
